transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I can’t stop dwelling on how my face and body look as I’m aging, and it’s making me avoid things I used to do without thinking. It has gotten to a point where it's really starting to disrupt my daily life, so I felt like I needed to talk to someone.

When you avoid things, is it mainly because you feel very anxious about being judged or embarrassed in social situations, or because you’re preoccupied that specific parts of your appearance look flawed or abnormal? Which of those feels closer to what’s driving this most of the time?

It is definitely because of how I look, rather than just being anxious about socializing. I am completely fixated on the sagging lines around my mouth and how my neck is starting to droop, making it feel like my whole face is collapsing. It makes me feel so old and worn-out that I simply can't bear the thought of anyone seeing me.

Do you think these changes in your appearance might be exaggerated in your mind, or are you completely certain they look as bad as you believe? Have other people told you they don’t notice the problem or that it looks minor?

My husband and coworkers constantly tell me they don't see any flaws and that I look fine, but I just can't believe them. When I look in the mirror, the sagging and collapsing of my face feel completely undeniable and severe. I am absolutely certain it looks as bad as I think, which makes it impossible to accept their reassurance.

Has any doctor or dermatologist told you there is no significant problem with your appearance, and if so, do you still believe with complete certainty that your face is severely deformed? Or are you more worried in general about having a serious physical problem despite normal reassurance?

Yes, my primary care doctor did a full physical exam and found everything to be completely normal, but I still can't help but see my face sagging and collapsing. I'm not worried about having a medical illness or a serious physical disease; my concern is strictly about how old, worn-out, and drooping my face and neck look.

Do you ever think there is even a small chance that your appearance concerns might be exaggerated, or are you completely certain your face is severely deformed despite what others say? Has this belief ever changed at all?

No, I really don't think I'm exaggerating because it feels completely real to me. When I look in the mirror, the sagging lines and my drooping neck are just so obvious and undeniable. Even if others say they don't see it, I am convinced everyone else is noticing how collapsed and worn-out my face looks.
Do you spend a lot of time checking mirrors, trying to hide or fix these areas, or comparing your appearance with other people? About how many hours a day do these thoughts and behaviors take up?

Yes, every morning I lose nearly an hour in front of the mirror putting on and wiping off makeup, zooming in on my face with my phone, and changing outfits to hide my neck and arms. I also constantly ask my husband if I look "too old" before I can even force myself out the door. These routines and thoughts take up so much of my day that I'm often late for work or end up canceling my plans altogether.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, false belief that her face and neck are severely deformed/abnormal despite repeated reassurance from others and a normal medical evaluation. The belief is circumscribed to appearance, held with delusional conviction, and accompanied by repetitive appearance-checking and marked functional impairment, supporting body dysmorphic disorder with absent insight/delusional beliefs, coded here under other persistent delusional disorders per the provided candidate set.
